plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid strategy for a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, which for n=3 gives 2/3 of value. My value is $9, so optimal bid ≈ $6.00. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitive.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal strategy in a first-price auction is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3. This balances the probability of winning against the profit margin. My value is $20, so I'll bid approximately $13.3 to maximize expected profit while still having a reasonable chance to win.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, i.e., 2/3 * value. My value is $20, so I should bid approximately $13.30 to balance winning probability against overpaying. This maximizes expected profit given optimal competitor behavior.
